title: Section 1: Narrative Tenses (Multiple Choice)
inst: Choose the correct verb tense (Past Simple, Past Continuous, or Past Perfect) to complete the story and the sentences.
theory:
Narrative Tenses Review:
- Past Simple: Main, completed, and consecutive actions in the past.
- Past Continuous: Long actions or actions in progress that were interrupted (while, when).
- Past Perfect: The 'oldest action', which happened BEFORE another action in the past (by the time, already, after).

items.q: 1. I ___ down the street when I suddenly heard a loud noise.
items.why: Action in progress interrupted by the noise (Past Continuous).

items.q: 2. By the time we arrived at the cinema, the movie ___.
items.why: The movie started BEFORE we arrived (Past Perfect).

items.q: 3. Yesterday, I woke up, ___ a quick shower, and left for work.
items.why: Sequence of short, consecutive past actions (Past Simple).

items.q: 4. While Sarah ___ her homework, her brother was playing video games.
items.why: Two actions in progress at the same time using 'while' (Past Continuous).

title: Section 2: The Bad Day (Story Completion)
inst: Write the verb in brackets in the correct narrative tense (Past Simple, Past Continuous, or Past Perfect).
theory: Pay attention to the context of the story to decide which tense to use.

items.q: 1. Last Monday, I ___ (have) a terrible day at the office.
items.why: Finished past action that introduces the story: had.

items.q: 2. I was exhausted because I ___ (not / sleep) well the night before.
items.why: Action that happened BEFORE Monday: hadn't slept / had not slept.

items.q: 3. While I ___ (prepare) a coffee in the kitchen, my boss called me.
items.why: Long interrupted action: was preparing.

items.q: 4. He asked me for the report, but I realized I ___ (forget) it at home!
items.why: Realized something that had happened BEFORE: had forgotten.

title: Section 1: Choose the Relative Pronoun
inst: Choose the correct relative pronoun (who, which, whose, where, when) for each sentence.
theory:
Relative Clauses Review:
- Who / That: For people.
- Which / That: For things or animals.
- Where: For places.
- When: For time.
- Whose: To indicate possession.

items.q: 1. That is the doctor ___ treated me when I broke my arm.
items.why: Refers to a person (the doctor).

items.q: 2. I can't find the folder ___ has all the important documents.
items.why: Refers to a thing (the folder).

items.q: 3. This is the hospital ___ my grandfather worked for 30 years.
items.why: Refers to a place where an action occurs (the hospital).

items.q: 4. Do you know the girl ___ brother won the gold medal?
items.why: Indicates possession: the girl's brother (whose).

title: Section 2: Combine the Sentences
inst: Combine the two sentences into one using a Relative Pronoun. Do not repeat the subject or the object!
theory:
Example:
The man is angry. His car is broken. -> The man whose car is broken is angry.

items.q:
1. The smartphone is very expensive. I bought it yesterday. (Use WHICH or THAT)
-> The smartphone ____________________________ is very expensive.
items.why: which/that I bought yesterday

items.q:
2. I met a woman. She works as a software engineer. (Use WHO or THAT)
-> I met a woman ____________________________.
items.why: who/that works as a software engineer

items.q:
3. That is the cafe. We had our first date there. (Use WHERE)
-> That is the cafe ____________________________.
items.why: where we had our first date

title: Section 1: Modals in Context
inst: Choose the correct modal verb to complete each sentence, paying attention to the context (obligation, prohibition, advice, or lack of obligation).
theory:
Modals Review:
- Must / Have to: Obligation (rules or necessity).
- Mustn't: Strict prohibition (do not do it).
- Don't have to: No obligation (you can do it if you want, but it's not necessary).
- Should / Ought to: Advice or recommendations.

items.q: 1. The sign says 'Private Property'. You ___ enter this area.
items.why: It is a strict prohibition indicated by a sign.

items.q: 2. Tomorrow is Sunday! I ___ wake up early.
items.why: Lack of obligation; it is not necessary to wake up early.

items.q: 3. You look very tired and sick. I think you ___ go to the doctor.
items.why: It is strong advice or a recommendation.

items.q: 4. In most offices, employees ___ wear a tie. It's the company rule.
items.why: It is an external obligation imposed by company rules.

title: Section 2: The Mega Integration (Key Word Transformations)
inst: The final challenge! Rewrite the sentences using the word in capital letters without changing the meaning. These sentences mix Past Tenses, Relatives, and Modals.
theory: Instructions: Use everything you have learned. Do not change the word in brackets.

items.q:
1. It is strictly prohibited for the students who study here to use phones.
-> The students who study here ____________________________ phones. (MUSTN'T)
items.why: mustn't use (Combines relatives with prohibition).

items.q:
2. My advice for the man whose car broke down is to take a taxi.
-> The man whose car broke down ____________________________ a taxi. (SHOULD)
items.why: should take (Combines relatives with advice).

items.q:
3. It was not necessary for me to read the book that the teacher recommended.
-> I ____________________________ the book that the teacher recommended. (HAVE)
items.why: didn't have to read (Combines lack of obligation in the PAST with a relative clause).

items.q:
4. While the doctor was examining the patient, it was a rule to wear gloves.
-> While the doctor was examining the patient, he ____________________________ gloves. (HAD)
items.why: had to wear (Combines past continuous with past obligation).

title: Exercise 1: Choose the Correct Future Form
inst: Read the contexts carefully and choose the most natural future form (will, going to, or Present Continuous). Pay attention to the evidence or the type of plan!
theory:
A. Expressing the Future (Will vs. Going to vs. Present Continuous)

In English, we don't have just one future tense. We choose the structure based on the context and our intentions.

  • WILL + Infinitive: Used for spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking (e.g., "The phone is ringing, I will answer it!"), promises, and predictions based on personal opinions/beliefs (e.g., "I think people will live on Mars").
  • BE GOING TO + Infinitive: Used for intentions and plans already made before speaking (e.g., "I am going to study architecture next year"), and predictions based on present evidence (e.g., "Look at those black clouds! It is going to rain").
  • PRESENT CONTINUOUS (am/is/are + -ing): Used for fixed arrangements. This means a plan that is 100% confirmed, usually with a specific time, place, or other people involved. (e.g., "I am meeting the doctor tomorrow at 5 PM").

items.q: 1. A: 'We don't have any milk left!' B: 'Really? I ___ to the supermarket right now.'
items.why: Spontaneous decision made at the moment of speaking (will)

items.q: 2. I can't meet you on Saturday. I ___ tennis with Sarah. We booked the court.
items.why: Fixed arrangement already booked (Present Continuous)

items.q: 3. Do you think people ___ on Mars in the year 2050?
items.why: Prediction based on opinion (will)

items.q: 4. A: 'The bag looks very heavy, let me help you.' B: 'Thanks! I ___ the small one.'
items.why: Spontaneous decision / offer (will)

items.q: 5. My flatmate and I ___ a party next Friday. We have already invited 20 people.
items.why: Fixed arrangement already confirmed (Present Continuous)

items.q: 6. I feel terrible. My stomach hurts a lot. I think I ___ sick.
items.why: Prediction based on present evidence (going to)

items.q: 7. I promise I ___ anyone your secret.
items.why: Promise (will / won't)

items.q: 8. Next week is my mother's birthday. I ___ her flowers, but I haven't gone to the shop yet.
items.why: Plan or intention decided before speaking (going to)

items.q: 9. Look at the terrible traffic! We ___ the start of the movie.
items.why: Prediction based on present evidence (going to)

items.q: 10. We have our tickets ready! We ___ the 8:00 AM train tomorrow morning.
items.why: Fixed arrangement with tickets ready (Present Continuous)

items.q: 11. I am sure that renewable energy ___ cheaper in the future.
items.why: Prediction based on belief (will)

items.q: 12. A: 'I forgot my wallet!' B: 'Don't worry, I ___ for the coffee.'
items.why: Spontaneous decision / offer (will)

items.q: 13. My sister ___ from university on Friday at 10 AM.
items.why: Fixed arrangement with a specific day and time (Present Continuous)

items.q: 14. Look at the battery, it's at 1%! My phone ___.
items.why: Prediction based on present evidence (going to)

items.q: 15. Next month, the company ___ a new smart watch.
items.why: Plan or intention (going to)

title: Exercise 2: First Conditional (Will vs. Modals)
inst: Complete the First Conditional sentences. Does it need a future prediction (will / won't) or a modal verb for advice or rules (must, should, don't have to, can)? Write both verb forms separated by a comma (e.g., is, will go).
theory:
B. The First Conditional (Real & Possible Situations)

Conditionals are "If" sentences. They describe the result of a certain condition. The First Conditional is used to talk about real and highly possible situations in the future.

Structure: If + Present Simple, ... Will + Infinitive

  • Example: "If we recycle more plastic, we will help the environment." (This is a real possibility).
  • Negative: "If she doesn't study, she won't pass the exam."

C. The Bridge: First Conditional + Modal Verbs

We don't always have to use "will" in the result clause. We can use Modal Verbs to give rules, permission, or advice based on a condition!

Structure: If + Present Simple, ... Modal Verb (must / should / can / have to) + Infinitive

  • Advice: "If you have a fever, you should stay at home."
  • Obligation/Rule: "If you visit the hospital, you must be quiet." / "If he wants the job, he has to send his CV."
  • Permission: "If you finish your homework, you can play video games."

items.q: 1. If the weather ___ (be) good tomorrow, we ___ (go) to the beach. (Prediction)
a: is, will go
is, 'll go
If the weather is good tomorrow, we will go to the beach.
If the weather is good tomorrow, we'll go to the beach.
items.why: Review First Conditional structure for predictions (will)

items.q: 2. If you ___ (feel) tired, you ___ (take) a break. (Advice)
a: feel, should take
If you feel tired, you should take a break.
items.why: Review First Conditional using a modal verb for advice (should)

items.q: 3. If students ___ (want) to pass the exam, they ___ (study) hard. (Obligation)
a: want, must study
want, have to study
If students want to pass the exam, they must study hard.
If students want to pass the exam, they have to study hard.
items.why: Review First Conditional using a modal verb for obligation (must / have to)

items.q: 4. If she ___ (not/hurry), she ___ (miss) the bus! (Prediction)
a: doesn't hurry, will miss
does not hurry, will miss
doesn't hurry, 'll miss
If she doesn't hurry, she will miss the bus!
If she does not hurry, she will miss the bus!
If she doesn't hurry, she'll miss the bus!
items.why: Review First Conditional negative structure for predictions (won't / will)

items.q: 5. If you ___ (finish) your vegetables, you ___ (eat) some chocolate. (Permission)
a: finish, can eat
If you finish your vegetables, you can eat some chocolate.
items.why: Review First Conditional using a modal verb for permission (can)

items.q: 6. If it ___ (rain) tomorrow, you ___ (not/have to) water the garden. (No obligation)
a: rains, don't have to
rains, do not have to
If it rains tomorrow, you don't have to water the garden.
If it rains tomorrow, you do not have to water the garden.
items.why: Review First Conditional using a modal verb for lack of obligation (don't have to)

items.q: 7. If we ___ (use) less plastic, we ___ (protect) the ocean. (Prediction)
a: use, will protect
use, 'll protect
If we use less plastic, we will protect the ocean.
If we use less plastic, we'll protect the ocean.
items.why: Review First Conditional structure for predictions (will)

items.q: 8. If you ___ (see) a red traffic light, you ___ (stop) your car immediately. (Strict Rule)
a: see, must stop
If you see a red traffic light, you must stop your car immediately.
items.why: Review First Conditional using a modal verb for a strict rule (must)

items.q: 9. If we ___ (not/protect) the forests, many animals ___ (lose) their homes. (Prediction)
a: don't protect, will lose
do not protect, will lose
don't protect, 'll lose
If we don't protect the forests, many animals will lose their homes.
If we do not protect the forests, many animals will lose their homes.
If we don't protect the forests, many animals'll lose their homes.
items.why: Review First Conditional negative structure for predictions (will)

items.q: 10. If the new software ___ (have) bugs, you ___ (report) it to the IT department immediately. (Strict Rule)
a: has, must report
has, have to report
If the new software has bugs, you must report it to the IT department immediately.
If the new software has bugs, you have to report it to the IT department immediately.
items.why: Review First Conditional using a modal verb for a strict rule (must)

items.q: 11. If you ___ (buy) a smart speaker, you ___ (control) the lights with your voice. (Permission/Ability)
a: buy, can control
If you buy a smart speaker, you can control the lights with your voice.
items.why: Review First Conditional using a modal verb for permission or ability (can)

items.q: 12. If they ___ (want) to travel to Europe, they ___ (save) money first. (Advice)
a: want, should save
If they want to travel to Europe, they should save money first.
items.why: Review First Conditional using a modal verb for advice (should)

title: Exercise 3: Key Word Transformations
inst: Rewrite the sentences keeping the exact same meaning. Use the word in brackets. This exercise mixes the First Conditional, futures, and modals!

items.q: 1. I advise you to talk to the manager if you have a problem. (SHOULD) -> If you have a problem, you ____________________ to the manager.
a: should talk
If you have a problem, you should talk to the manager.
items.why: Use should to give advice

items.q: 2. The company will probably fire him if he is late again. (WILL) -> If he is late again, the company ____________________ him.
a: will probably fire
If he is late again, the company will probably fire him.
items.why: Use will for a likely future result

items.q: 3. It is strictly prohibited to use smartphones if you are driving. (MUSTN'T) -> If you are driving, you ____________________ smartphones.
a: mustn't use
must not use
If you are driving, you mustn't use smartphones.
If you are driving, you must not use smartphones.
items.why: Use mustn't for prohibitions

items.q: 4. I plan to travel to Japan next year. I have the intention. (GOING) -> I ____________________ to Japan next year.
a: am going to travel
'm going to travel
I am going to travel to Japan next year.
I'm going to travel to Japan next year.
items.why: Use going to for plans and intentions

items.q: 5. It is not necessary for you to wear a tie if you work on Fridays. (HAVE) -> If you work on Fridays, you ____________________ a tie.
a: don't have to wear
do not have to wear
If you work on Fridays, you don't have to wear a tie.
If you work on Fridays, you do not have to wear a tie.
items.why: Use don't have to for lack of obligation

items.q: 6. Look at those black clouds! I am 100% sure it will rain soon. (GOING) -> Look at those black clouds! It ____________________ soon.
a: is going to rain
's going to rain
Look at those black clouds! It is going to rain soon.
Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain soon.
items.why: Use going to for predictions with present evidence

items.q: 7. We have an appointment to meet the doctor at 4 PM tomorrow. (ARE) -> We ____________________ the doctor at 4 PM tomorrow.
a: are meeting
're meeting
We are meeting the doctor at 4 PM tomorrow.
We're meeting the doctor at 4 PM tomorrow.
items.why: Use Present Continuous for fixed arrangements

items.q: 8. It is a strict company rule to wear a safety helmet if you enter the factory. (MUST) -> If you enter the factory, you ____________________ a safety helmet.
a: must wear
If you enter the factory, you must wear a safety helmet.
items.why: Use must for strict rules and obligations

items.q: 9. I strongly advise you to check the internet connection if the app fails. (SHOULD) -> If the app fails, you ____________________ the internet connection.
a: should check
If the app fails, you should check the internet connection.
items.why: Use should to give advice

items.q: 10. It is not necessary for her to buy a new laptop if this one works fine. (HAVE) -> If this one works fine, she ____________________ a new laptop.
a: doesn't have to buy
does not have to buy
If this one works fine, she doesn't have to buy a new laptop.
If this one works fine, she does not have to buy a new laptop.
items.why: Use doesn't have to for lack of obligation

title: Exercise 4: The Editor's Challenge (Spot the B1 Mistake)
inst: There is ONE grammar mistake in each sentence related to future tenses or the First Conditional. Find it and write the correct sentence.

items.q: 1. If I will see him at the party, I will tell him the good news.
a: If I see him at the party, I will tell him the good news.
If I see him at the party, I'll tell him the good news.
items.why: Remember the First Conditional rules: do not use 'will' directly after 'if'

items.q: 2. Look at that tree! It will fall down!
a: Look at that tree! It is going to fall down!
Look at that tree! It's going to fall down!
items.why: Review future tenses for predictions based on present evidence

items.q: 3. I promise I am going to help you with your project tomorrow.
a: I promise I will help you with your project tomorrow.
I promise I'll help you with your project tomorrow.
items.why: Review future tenses for promises

items.q: 4. If you have a headache, you will take an aspirin.
a: If you have a headache, you should take an aspirin.
items.why: Use a modal verb for advice instead of a future prediction

items.q: 5. If the robot will break, we will call the engineer.
a: If the robot breaks, we will call the engineer.
If the robot breaks, we'll call the engineer.
items.why: Remember the First Conditional rules: do not use 'will' directly after 'if'

items.q: 6. I think that flying cars are going to be normal in 100 years.
a: I think that flying cars will be normal in 100 years.
I think flying cars will be normal in 100 years.
items.why: Use will for predictions based on opinion (I think...)

title: Reading: The Future of Smart Cities
inst: Read the article about life in 2050 and answer the questions below.
theory:
The Future of Smart Cities

By the year 2050, over 70% of the world's population will live in urban areas. To manage this growth, governments are going to build "Smart Cities". These cities will use artificial intelligence and renewable energy to improve our lifestyle and fight climate change.

In a Smart City, the house where you live will be completely automated. If you leave the house, the smart devices will automatically turn off the lights and lower the heating. If this system works perfectly, you won't have to worry about wasting electricity. Furthermore, public transport will be self-driving. If everyone uses self-driving electric buses, the air in our cities will be much cleaner.

However, some experts are worried about security. If technology controls everything, we must protect our digital networks. If a hacker attacks the city's network, the entire transport system will collapse. Technology gives us solutions, but if we want to be safe, we should be prepared.

items.q: 1. According to the text, what is the main purpose of building Smart Cities?
2. Find and write down a First Conditional sentence that uses "will/won't".
a: If you leave the house, the smart devices will automatically turn off the lights and lower the heating.
If this system works perfectly, you won't have to worry about wasting electricity.
If everyone uses self-driving electric buses, the air in our cities will be much cleaner.
If a hacker attacks the city's network, the entire transport system will collapse.
items.why: First Conditional: If + Present Simple, will / won't + infinitive

items.q: 3. Find and write down a First Conditional sentence that uses a Modal Verb for advice or obligation.
a: If technology controls everything, we must protect our digital networks.
If we want to be safe, we should be prepared.
Technology gives us solutions, but if we want to be safe, we should be prepared.
items.why: First Conditional with a modal verb (must / should)

items.q: 4. What is the relative clause used in the second paragraph to describe the house?
a: where you live
the house where you live
items.why: Relative clause with where (for places)

title: The Environmental Action Plan
inst: Work with your teacher. Imagine you are creating an action plan for your city to fight climate change. Together, write a short paragraph proposing 4 changes. You MUST use the First Conditional combined with future results or modal verbs (e.g., "If we ban plastic bags, we will...", "If citizens want a cleaner city, they must...").
